lines: The parcel that slid down the library ramp after the first mystery was waiting beside the five-star map.
There is the parcel, beside the map. The label says Mia, Sol and Tavi. It is for us! Help me move it along the glowing floor path to the yellow reading mat.
You guided the parcel to our mat. Inside is a Moon Lantern! The card asks us to take it to the balcony before the first evening star.
The friends followed the card towards the balcony. A small door blocked the way. The lantern was too wide to fit through it.
Hello! I’m Pax. We can take the lantern apart, carry every part through, and build the whole lantern again. First, tap the covered lantern. Each tap will uncover one part.
That is our whole lantern. Every part is here, with no gap and no extra piece. Now we know what we must build again.
The lantern came apart into four pieces. All four waited beside the small door.
The door is narrow, so we must carry one lantern part at a time. Let’s move all four through, and not carry any part twice.
All four lantern parts went through the small door. Each part moved once, and none was left behind.
Pax laid four lantern-picture cards beside a round plan frame.
Each card shows one same-size part. Match every curved part to its place. The four parts must fill the lantern plan with no gap and no part on top of another.
All four lantern pictures fit the plan. There is no gap, and no part covers another. Together, they fill the same whole lantern.
All four lantern parts waited beside the empty round frame.
Put every part into the frame. Use each part once, and leave none behind.
We did it! All four parts fit together. The same whole lantern is back, and the tray is empty.
Pax put two pairs of lantern-part pictures on the balance table.
One pair shows lantern parts that are the same size. Look at both pairs before you choose.
Pair A has same-size lantern parts. Pair B has one big lantern part and one small one. Now Pax can use the four-part plan.
Mia placed three lantern parts in the round frame. One space was still empty. A lantern part and a triangle were nearby.
Which piece is part of this lantern? Choose it, turn its top upright, and fit it into the empty space.
The lantern part belongs in the gap. The triangle stays outside because it is not part of this lantern.
Pax held two lantern parts. The other two waited on the tray, so all four were still easy to see.
How many parts am I holding? Then tell me how many parts make the whole lantern.
Pax is holding two. Four parts make the whole lantern. We have all four, so we can rebuild it.
The friends reached the balcony before the first evening star. The four lantern parts were still separate. They needed to count the parts together before rebuilding the lantern.
Put one lantern part in each space. The plus signs mean we are joining the separate counted parts. Then choose how many parts there are altogether.

One part plus one part plus one part plus one part equals four parts. Equals means both sides count the same four parts. Then we joined the four parts and rebuilt one whole lantern. A blue moon picture lit up. Then a gold sun picture lit up. The two pictures began to take turns.

Here is the lesson. Addition joins separate counted groups without losing or repeating anything. One part plus one part plus one part plus one part equals four parts. The equals sign tells us that both sides count the same four parts. Then we fitted those four parts together to rebuild one whole lantern. This matters because addition helps us check how many things we have altogether, while a parts plan helps us build the whole correctly.
